prompt: What happens when this runs with name set to null?
choices: It does not compile - null cannot be compared with !=
explanation: && stops as soon as the answer is settled. name != null is false, so the whole condition is already false and name.length() is never evaluated - which is exactly what makes this null-check idiom safe. Writing & instead would evaluate both sides and throw.
hints: Does && always evaluate its right-hand side?
If the left side of && is false, can the answer still change?
